actions.text: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.

dimensions.assessment: Affects commercial air carrier passengers originating at U.S. airports and entities involved in airport security infrastructure.
dimensions.evidence: TSA collects passenger civil aviation security service fees (often referred to as the 9/11 security fee or passenger security fee) on air carrier passengers originating at airports in the United States.

dimensions.assessment: Changes the allocation of security fee revenues to fund equipment and checkpoint technology upgrades.
dimensions.evidence: allocates additional funding for the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) for aviation security, including checked baggage explosives detection equipment and security checkpoint technology.

dimensions.assessment: Directs $500 million annually to the Aviation Security Capital Fund and $250 million annually to the Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology Fund from fee collections.
dimensions.evidence: requires that the first $500 million collected in each fiscal year from passenger security fees be deposited into the Aviation Security Capital Fund. This is an increase from the currently required $250 million.

dimensions.assessment: Amends title 49, United States Code, establishes a new fund within the Department of Homeland Security, and modifies grant and funding authorities.
dimensions.evidence: There is established within the Department of Homeland Security a fund to be known as the Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology Fund

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent funding requirements beginning in fiscal year 2026 and allows retroactive use of funds for projects dating back to January 1, 2023.
dimensions.evidence: Beginning in fiscal year 2026, and for each fiscal year thereafter, the first $500,000,000 derived from fees received under section 44940(a)(1) shall be available

missing_information: Specific details on the total amount of passenger security fees collected annually beyond the specified $750 million threshold.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill redirects existing passenger security fee collections to increase annual funding for the Aviation Security Capital Fund from $250 million to $500 million and establishes a new $250 million Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology Fund, permanently altering how these aviation fee revenues are distributed.
